manifest.notes:
Mandatory two-step verification: administrators can require two-step verification (MFA) for the whole
organization, by role or for specific users, from *Administration → Settings → Access security*.

- Grace period of 0 to 30 days from the first time the user signs in while it is required; during it, a notice
  with a countdown. When it ends, the user can only open the *Set up two-step verification* wizard (QR code, app code
  and recovery codes) before using NetPilot. The policy preview tells how many users it affects and warns if it would
  lock you out.
- Recovery codes: ten single-use codes when it is turned on (stored hashed), to sign in if the phone is lost;
  they can be regenerated from the profile. Signing in with one notifies the user, is logged and lets them set up the
  app again.
- Reset a user's MFA (on their page, *Security* tab): asks for a reason and to confirm your identity, closes
  their sessions and makes them set it up at their next sign-in. Turning it on, turning it off, resetting it, using a
  recovery code and changing the policy are recorded in the change log.
- Corporate sign-in: LDAP users use NetPilot's verification like local users. With OIDC the provider's
  verification (Entra ID, Google…) is trusted by default; the policy can also require NetPilot's code.
- API tokens do not go through two-step verification (they are not interactive) and keep working. RMM identity
  confirmation does not change and does not accept recovery codes. The policy does not apply in the demo.
- Safer: an app code cannot be used twice; sign-in limits failed attempts (10 in 10 minutes); turning on
  verification no longer replaces an active one without confirming your identity and the server no longer accepts a
  secret sent by the browser; changing another user's password asks you to confirm your identity, is logged and closes
  their sessions; LDAP users can turn verification off; netpilotctl reset-password --disable-2fa also deletes the
  recovery codes, closes the user's sessions and is logged. Closing a user's sessions also cuts what they had open in
  RMM (terminals, remote desktop, download and RustDesk links) and the backup links.
- The change history of user accounts (including the reasons for a reset) is only shown to administrators.

User page (*Administration → Users*): each user has a page with *Summary*, *Access*, *Security* and *History*.
The list shows the two-step verification status (enabled, required with its deadline, blocked, from the provider)
and a summary of their access.

Access by sections, locations and departments: besides the role, *Access* on the user page can limit what they
see, without a license and always enforced by the server (a request outside their access answers 403 or 404):

- Sections and areas: the sections of the side menu (Inventory, Warehouse, Catalog, Network, Connectivity,
  Operations, Documentation, RMM, Field, Maps, Integrations, Audit) and their areas (for example, *Warehouse* without
  *Licenses*, or *Operations → Tickets*). Ticking a whole section includes its future areas. The menu, Ctrl+K search,
  help, dashboard and record pages only show what is theirs; a page of another section shows *No access to this
  section*. Audit, Maps and Field show the names of everything, without links to the rest, and form pickers show the
  names of sites, companies, models, devices and endpoints of other sections without opening their pages.
- Locations and companies: locations at any level of the tree (each one includes everything below it, also what
  is created later) and/or companies. Before, this could only be set up with the SSO or MSP module.
- Departments (*Administration → Departments*): warehouse items and warehouses, software licenses, documentation
  shelves and books, endpoints, devices, racks, tickets, credentials and quotes can belong to one or more departments.
  A user limited to, for example, *Sound* only sees what belongs to Sound; what has no department is only seen by
  users without a limit. Stock levels, units, movements, pages, RMM, attachments, journal and history follow the
  object they depend on. *Departments* column, filter and bulk action in the lists.
- The three combine with each other and with the role. Administrators see everything.

Users limited by location or company: restrictions are always enforced, with any license. A limited user cannot
create anything above their location or move, delete or change the company of their site, and does not see the
regions above it. Every route of the application (reads, writes, notifications, exports, reports, labels, AI
assistant…) has been reviewed so they neither see nor touch anything of other locations; organization-wide features
that cannot be limited (Discovery, Connectors, Automation, Change management, Time machine, Quotes) are not
available to them and shared catalogs (risk and CVE, configuration rules, quote price list, RMM script library and
permissions) are read-only. The full JSON copy (*Integrations → Export*) is for administrators only.

Wake-on-LAN (rmm module): *Power on (Wake-on-LAN)* in the *Power* menu of the endpoint page (also without an
agent, if its MAC is known), on a device page and for several endpoints at once from *Inventory → Endpoints*.

- The packet is sent by an online agent of the same site (of the same subnet when there is one) and, if there is
  none, by the server itself with a directed broadcast to the subnet (ports 9 and 7, configurable in *RMM →
  Settings*). Before sending you can see which way it will go.
- If the endpoint has an agent, NetPilot waits for it to reconnect (10 minutes by default) and tells you: *online at
  10:31* or that it has not come back.
- New rmm.wol permission (editors and administrators), a limit of endpoints powered on per minute, blocked by the
  emergency switch and recorded in the RMM activity. The sending endpoint needs agent 1.8.1. In Docker, sending from
  the server needs network_mode: host.

Pages with many tabs: tabs are grouped in drop-down menus when there are more than eight. On an endpoint with an
agent: *Summary · Monitoring · Inventory ▾ · Tools ▾ · Terminal · Scripts · Remote desktop ▾ · More ▾*. The active
tab shows on its group, they work with the keyboard and on mobile they become a single drop-down; ?tab= links keep
working.

Search: in search (Ctrl+K) help articles come last, after the results and actions.

Fixes: CSV export of Documentation shelves; the audit report PDF with many object types; the *Administrator 2FA*
compliance check counts the OIDC provider's verification and a policy that requires it; arrow keys on tabs;
untranslated texts in some RMM and Licenses errors; PUT /settings no longer changes settings that have their own
page (such as RMM security); in the Warehouse, creating an item without a SKU from the form no longer fails and an
empty tag in a receipt through the API is no longer stored as «None».

RMM agent 1.8.1: adds sending Wake-on-LAN (wol/1). 1.8.0 agents keep working, but cannot power on other
endpoints until they are updated.

Licenses: there are no new modules; mandatory verification and access by sections, locations and departments
are part of the core. Wake-on-LAN is part of the rmm module.

Help: new and updated articles in English and Spanish (two-step verification, user access, departments,
Wake-on-LAN, grouped tabs).

Database: migrations 0022 (mandatory two-step verification and recovery codes), 0023 (sections of each user)
and 0024 (departments); they are applied automatically when updating. The web update makes a backup first; if you
update by hand, make one before with netpilotctl backup.
